title: MATH 3042 Statistics · Unit 3
subtitle: Probability and counting, with Lab 3 (charts in R) and Lab 4 (simulations), preparing for Quiz 4 Part 1 and Quiz 5
description: Unit 3, probability from the ground up: random experiments, sample spaces and events, the classical and relative-frequency definitions and the law of large numbers, the fundamental counting rule with factorials, permutations and combinations on a deck of cards, the complement and addition rules, conditional probability and independence read off a two-way table, the multiplication rule, and Bayes' rule on a tree diagram. Plus the two labs of the week: Lab 3's pie, bar, stem, histogram, ogive and scatter charts of the survey data in R, and Lab 4's sample() and replicate() simulations, with Quiz 4 Part 2 as posted. Every example in the notes is worked with the instructor's arithmetic from the filled pages; the 28 posted practice problems worked; clickable sample spaces, a counting calculator, a two-way table, a Bayes tree and a simulation lab; a mock quiz and a formula sheet.
intro:
:::quiz Which quiz tests Unit 3
The quizzes follow one pattern: **Part 1, paper and pencil** (10 marks) on the previous lecture unit and **Part 2, RStudio** (10 marks) on the previous lab. Quiz 3 (posted solutions, Oct 8) was therefore Unit 2 + Lab 3, not this unit. By the same pattern, assumed here and not yet confirmed by a posted paper, Unit 3 is tested in **Quiz 4 Part 1** (counting, the NOT / OR / AND rules, a two-way table, a Bayes tree, with a scientific calculator and its nPr / nCr keys), and its rules return in **Quiz 5** beside Lab 5's conditional probability in R. Quiz 4 Part 2 (posted) was a Lab 4 simulation: a `sample()` / `replicate()` match, a histogram of X, and an "is X unusual?" verdict; it is worked in the Lab 4 lesson. The Unit 3 notes are now posted filled, and every worked example here carries the instructor's own numbers.
:::
